image.alt: Ron watches Tar'Mo approach through a moonlit corridor at Peak Temple, his cursed right hand visible

paragraphs: 再次睜開眼，一天已經過去了。對於尖頂寺的運作方式，龍恩還有所掌握---只要將壞東西擋在寺外，寺內按照規則走就沒事。廢棄的倉庫終究是廢棄的倉庫，也不會突然有個什麼閒雜人等躲在裡面的吧？更何況，龍恩也不是什麼閒雜人等，他終究是尖頂寺的一份子：離開尖頂寺前是，離開尖頂寺後也還是，就像當時在麥克嵩的比武大會時，他「尖頂寺的龍恩」這個名號。名符其實。
站起身，筋骨像是幾千年沒活絡一般喀喀作響，差點就散了，但龍恩很快就恢復了矯健的手腳，輕巧推開了門。夜已深，看來他這一口氣睡了有一天半，甚至近兩天的時間。遠處走廊上傳來僧人的腳步聲，讓龍恩回想起自己在這裡的時光。但現在有比回憶還更重要的事。
他的身體，似乎有股說不出的渴望，但是究竟渴望什麼，龍恩也說不上來。但他隱約感覺到，答案就在尖頂寺。也許他被傳送來這裡，是有某種力量暗地為他做了決定也說不定。但到底渴望什麼呢？
自從出發冒險，遇上了這群還能稱得上「夥伴」的各種生物後，龍恩不再需要擔心安危與吃住，算是能達成最基本的生活條件。偶爾也發生些有趣的事，在酒館見識各種怪人和事件，或是看看那些貴族們都過著什麼生活。有時候也有些光怪陸離，難以描述的怪事，像是差點喝下味道詭異的藥水、聽不懂的歌謠，或是會唱歌又會魔法的奇怪女性。這世界還有太多莫名其妙的事了。
當然，還有蘿琳。不知道他現在過得怎麼樣？在解救了他的靈魂後，蘿琳應該一切安好吧？

說起來，這⋯⋯這隻奇妙的手臂怎麼來的，龍恩完全不記得。總覺得好像做了一場模模糊糊的夢，醒來後自己的手就變這樣了。夥伴們似乎常常對著他大吼大叫，覺得是髒東西，要他把這手給砍掉之類的。慢爆則十分喜歡這隻手，也許和拉索斯教有些關係也說不定。這手也過得挺坎坷的，被金鏈綑綁限制，抑制他的能力。不懂，手臂這麼強，幹嘛抑制他的能力呢？想著想著，龍恩感到眼窩有些刺癢感。他自然地用那隻手抓了抓眼睛，卻摸到些溫熱的血。嗯？被蟲子咬了嗎？還是睡覺時擦傷了？再說吧。
夜幕中，寧靜的走廊上，一名年紀不大的僧人獨自從遠方朝著他走來。年紀大約和他剛進尖頂寺時差不多吧，不過那時候有塔爾莫領著他，因此龍恩再怎麼懵懂，也沒像這名師弟這樣⋯⋯單純。龍恩不由自主的看向師弟的臉，目光聚焦在他的雙眼。師弟停下了腳步，看起來有些不知所措。
然後龍恩斷片了。
「米多莉，那你怎麼想呢？」對於小雪的發言，羅賓遜主教愣住了幾秒，才吐出這句話。
「米多莉做什麼決定，我都願意配合，就算要我跟著留下來也沒問題。」在米多莉發言前，波就搶著回話，雙眼真摯地看向米多莉。「如果要繼續一起打敗拉索斯教，我也準備好了。」
「我很想同意，可是我們還有台北市議員的成員下落不明。」薩梅爾一手摸著酷爆的頭，一面看著米多莉。「米多莉，你說好要守護大家的，對吧？」
「龍恩解放巫妖的力量，可能對世界帶來毀滅性的打擊，但現在知道這件事的人太少，幾乎只有我們有機會阻止。」喜利搓著他的下巴思索著。「如果失敗，屆時津菈教和小雪也很難倖免於難。」
「這樣充斥著污穢的土地與宅邸，還是俐落地用把大火來淨化吧！」YHWH 一派輕鬆地看著湯普生爵士的宅邸，拿起手杖把玩，絲毫沒有注意到波用著嫌惡的眼神瞟了他一眼。
「小雪，我很感激你提出的這個機會，也很珍惜和你一起的時光。」米多莉轉過身。「這是屬於你的人生，不管最後你要留下來或是離開，我都支持。但是身為台北市議員的一份子，我有我的責任。龍恩也是我的夥伴，我不能就這樣放著不管。」
小雪輕輕點了點頭。「那我就在這裡先把宅邸打掃乾淨吧。」他微笑。「我等你回來唷。」小雪輕輕伸出手，翹起小拇指，等著米多莉。「說好了，這一次，不會再有人把我們分開了。」
「等我回來。」米多莉伸出小指，勾向小雪。「等我回來。」
再次接觸到地面，已是離開小雪後的兩天。方努爾市一如往常的人來人往，在羅賓遜主教的帶領下，大家順利地回到聖津菈大教堂。
「主教，後續就交給我吧，您先休息。」瑪莉修女向羅賓遜主教輕輕敬了個禮，主教則輕拍他的肩膀，然後走往辦公室的方向緩步前行。
「好啦，你們說這個魔法陣，在地下室對吧？」瑪莉回頭看向台北市議員。「你們可能不知道，但聖津菈大教堂的地下室很大喔，不知道要多久才能找到。就算找到了，要啟動傳送魔法，我聽說也需要研究一下，畢竟你們不是施術者，不一定能馬上看懂他當時是怎麼畫的。」
龍恩回神，身上滿是血跡。到底怎麼搞得這樣一塌糊塗？然後他才發現躺在眼前的，是方才看見的小師弟。他的眼窩是空的。然後龍恩才意識到自己兩隻手緊緊握著兩顆眼球。他慌忙地鬆開手。
這是什麼意思？
龍恩試圖把那兩顆眼珠塞回小師弟的眼窩，兩顆眼珠子歪歪斜斜地，很不對勁。然後他才發現小師弟已沒了生息。小師弟脖子上的咬痕、抓痕⋯⋯是他幹的嗎？放眼望去，也沒看見其他人影。聽見尖頂寺定時傳來的鐘聲，看來已過了午夜，不知道他斷片多久了。
儘管冒險了好一段時間，對於處理屍體這件事，龍恩還是覺得有些麻煩，除了那次在大學城將那個喊著要救蘿琳，卻讓人感到煩躁的年輕小屁孩以外。那個叫安德烈亞還是安德魯的歷史區區長的庭院剛好很適合挖洞，屍體一拋下去就搞定了。那現在這個小師弟的屍體又該怎麼辦。
唉算了，睡了快兩天的倉庫都沒被發現，就先丟倉庫裡去吧，味道稍微處理一下，應該不會被發現。
但那兩顆眼睛的話⋯⋯說實在，還真看不出這兩顆眼睛是要幹嘛的。當然，小師弟生前，這兩顆眼睛肯定是讓他用來看的，但現在呢？挖出來又要幹嘛？想著想著，龍恩突然感到眼窩發癢、眼睛乾澀。他想起曾聽過波和 YHWH 私下的談話。
當時他們討論到了某個巫妖的傳說。那名不知道叫「瓦」什麼的巫妖，好像有三件寶物，只要集齊了，就能變得很厲害。他的這隻酷酷的手，和前陣子在大學城找到的那本書，好像剛好是其中兩件。難不成，第三件就是眼睛？
所以是要自己挖掉眼睛，裝一顆還是兩顆別人的眼睛進去？怎麼聽怎麼荒謬。
收拾乾淨，龍恩從廢棄倉庫走了出來，悄聲的走回先前撞見小師弟的地方。他得確認那裡沒有留下什麼可疑的痕跡。要是被發現就不妙了。
有人，站在那裡。龍恩小心靠著牆壁，屏住呼吸。還是應該先下手為強好呢？
然而，在龍恩下決定前，那人走了過來。
月光下，塔爾莫曾經俊俏的臉，顯得比龍恩印象中的更蒼老。
「師弟啊！你終究也回來尖頂寺了。」塔爾莫迷人的微笑，比什麼都難解讀。

When he opened his eyes again, a day had passed. Ron still understood how Peak Temple worked: keep the bad things outside, follow the rules inside, and everything would be fine. An abandoned storeroom was just an abandoned storeroom; surely no suspicious stranger would suddenly be hiding there? Besides, Ron was hardly a stranger. He was part of Peak Temple. He had been before he left, and he still was afterward, just as he had called himself “Ron of Peak Temple” at the tournament in Macksohn. The name fit.

He stood up. His joints cracked as though they had lain idle for thousands of years, almost falling apart, but his limbs soon regained their agility, and he eased the door open. It was deep into the night. Apparently he had slept for a day and a half, perhaps nearly two days. The footsteps of monks in a distant corridor reminded him of his time here. But there were more pressing matters than memories.

His body seemed to harbor an indescribable craving, though he could not say what it wanted. He vaguely sensed that the answer lay within Peak Temple. Perhaps some hidden power had decided for him when he teleported here. But what exactly did he crave?

Since setting out on his adventures and meeting that assortment of creatures he could still call “companions,” Ron no longer had to worry about safety, food, or shelter. His basic needs were met. Sometimes interesting things happened: odd people and incidents in taverns, glimpses of how the nobles lived. Sometimes things were downright bizarre and hard to explain, like nearly drinking a strange-tasting potion, incomprehensible songs, or a peculiar woman who could both sing and use magic. There was still so much nonsense in this world.
And, of course, there was Roline. How was she doing now? After they had rescued her soul, she ought to be all right, shouldn't she?

Come to think of it... Ron could not remember how he had acquired this extraordinary arm. It felt as though he had woken from a hazy dream to find his hand like this. His companions often seemed to shout at him, calling it something foul and telling him to cut it off. Manbao, on the other hand, liked it very much; perhaps it had something to do with the Laxthos faith. The hand had endured its share of hardships, bound by a golden chain that suppressed its powers. He did not understand. Why suppress such a powerful arm? As he pondered, his eye sockets began to itch. Instinctively he scratched at his eyes with that hand, only to feel warm blood. Hm? An insect bite? Had he scratched himself in his sleep? He would deal with it later.

In the quiet corridor, a young monk approached alone through the darkness. He looked about the age Ron had been when he first entered Peak Temple. Back then, however, Ron had Tar'Mo to guide him. Naive as he had been, he had never been quite as... innocent as this junior. Without meaning to, Ron looked at the young monk's face, his gaze settling on the boy's eyes. The junior stopped, looking bewildered.
Then Ron blacked out.
“Midori, what do you think?” Bishop Robinson froze for a few seconds after Yuki's proposal before finally speaking.

“Whatever Midori decides, I'll go along with it. Even if that means staying here with her.” Before Midori could answer, Beau spoke up, looking at her with earnest eyes. “If we're going to keep fighting the Laxthos cult together, I'm ready for that too.”
“I'd like to agree, but some members of the Taipei City Councilors are still missing.” Samael stroked Kubao's head as he looked at Midori. “You promised to protect everyone, didn't you?”

“If Ron unleashes the lich's power, it could devastate the world. But so few people know about it that we're almost the only ones who have a chance of stopping him.” Siri rubbed his chin in thought. “If we fail, the Keinra church and Yuki will hardly be spared either.”

“A land and manor so steeped in filth ought to be cleansed with a good, brisk fire!” YHWH gazed casually at Syr Thompson's manor and toyed with his cane, entirely oblivious to Beau's disgusted glance.

“Yuki, I'm grateful for the opportunity you've offered, and I treasure our time together.” Midori turned around. “This is your life. Whether you choose to stay or leave, I support you. But as a member of the Taipei City Councilors, I have a responsibility. Ron is my companion too. I can't simply abandon him.”

Yuki nodded gently. “Then I'll stay here and clean up the manor first.” She smiled. “I'll wait for you to come back.” She held out her hand, little finger raised, waiting for Midori. “It's a promise. This time, no one will separate us again.”
“Wait for me.” Midori hooked her little finger around Yuki's. “Wait for me.”

By the time they stepped onto land again, two days had passed since they left Yuki. Fanaur was as bustling as ever. With Bishop Robinson leading the way, everyone returned safely to Saint Keinra Cathedral.
“Your Grace, leave the rest to me. Please get some rest.” Sister Mari bowed lightly to Bishop Robinson. He patted her shoulder and slowly made his way toward his office.

“All right, you said this magic circle is in the basement?” Mari turned back to the Taipei City Councilors. “You may not know this, but Saint Keinra Cathedral has a very large basement. Who knows how long it'll take to find it? Even once we do, I've heard that activating teleportation magic takes some study. You aren't the caster, after all, so you may not immediately understand how they drew it.”

Ron came to, covered in blood. How had he made such a mess? Then he noticed the young junior lying before him. His eye sockets were empty. Only then did Ron realize he was clutching an eyeball in each hand. He hastily let go.
What did this mean?

Ron tried to stuff the two eyes back into the junior's sockets. They sat crookedly, looking terribly wrong. Then he realized the boy was no longer breathing. The bites and scratches on his neck... had Ron done that? He looked around, but there was no one else in sight. The temple's regular bells sounded. It seemed to be past midnight. He had no idea how long he had blacked out.

Despite all his time adventuring, disposing of a body still seemed troublesome to Ron. There had been that annoying young brat in Great Citadel who kept insisting on saving Roline. The yard belonging to that history district head—Andrea, or Andrew, or whatever his name was—had been perfect for digging a hole. Tossing the body in had taken care of it. But what was he supposed to do with this young junior's body?

Oh, forget it. No one had discovered him in the storeroom where he had slept for nearly two days. He could leave the body there for now. Take care of the smell a little, and it probably wouldn't be found.

As for those two eyes... honestly, he could not see what they were for. While the junior was alive, of course, he had used them to see. But now? What was the point of digging them out? As he thought, Ron's eye sockets suddenly itched and his eyes felt dry. He remembered overhearing Beau and YHWH talking in private.

They had been discussing a legend about some lich. That lich, whose name began with “Va” or something, supposedly had three treasures. Collect all three, and you could become incredibly powerful. This cool hand of his and that book they had found in Great Citadel seemed to be two of them. Could the third be an eye?
So was he supposed to gouge out his own eyes and put one or two of someone else's in their place? It sounded absurd no matter how he thought about it.
After cleaning up, Ron left the abandoned storeroom and quietly returned to where he had encountered the junior. He had to make sure he had left no suspicious traces. Being discovered would be bad.
Someone was standing there. Ron pressed carefully against the wall and held his breath. Perhaps he should strike first?
Before he could decide, however, the figure came toward him.
In the moonlight, Tar'Mo's once-handsome face looked older than Ron remembered.
“Junior! You've come back to Peak Temple at last.” Tar'Mo's charming smile was harder to read than anything else.
